title: Distinguish 'field has limited capability' (warn, flag-gated) from 'field is not nameable' (always 400)
answers: Should a new search request validation always error or just warn?
When should a search field check be feature-flagged?
Pattern for rejecting invalid search request fields
body: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:toBleveSearchRequest runs a chain of request-field checks before executing a query (rejectInternalFields, validateTrashRequest, rejectTrashFieldsOnLiveSearch). The sort-capability check is off by default and only warns because it concerns a field whose capabilities merely fall short. rejectInternalFields and the trash-field checks are unconditional 400s because they concern a field the request may never name at all (internal index-only field, or a field that only deleted documents carry). When adding a new check here, decide which category it is: a capability shortfall gets a flag and a warning, a field that is categorically not usable in this context gets an unconditional bad-request error.
applies: Any new validation added to pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go's request-building path.

The sort-capability check is off by default and warns because the field's capabilities merely fall short; rejectInternalFields and trash-field checks are unconditional 400s because they concern fields the request may never name at all (internal index-only fields or fields only deleted documents carry). Applies to any new validation added to pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go's request-field checks.
